74% of participants wanted to explore clean energy careers. 56% asked how to start.

These are findings from UNDP and Goodwall’s conversations with more than 58,000 young people across over 180 countries. One participant described people travelling long distances just to charge their devices. With 655 million people still without electricity, that journey says a great deal about who can access the digital economy.

Today, we brought public and private sector partners together to discuss how to close the skills gap and bring clean energy jobs to places that need them most.

Renewable energy already employs 16.6 million people, but more than 85% of those jobs are concentrated in five countries and regions. The talent is far more widely distributed.

Young people proposed businesses ranging from solar-powered kitchens to sustainable energy consultancies. They also asked for practical ways to learn the skills those ideas require. UNDP’s upcoming Sustainable Energy Academy will offer more than 40 hours of modules spanning energy finance and governance, access and efficiency, data and technology, and the climate-energy nexus.

As a young man from the Philippines told us: “Invest not only in clean energy technologies, but also in the young people who build them. Because when we power communities with clean energy, we don't just light homes, we ignite opportunities.”

Every year of delay leaves communities without reliable power and holds back the people ready to build a cleaner energy future.

Tomorrow, UNDP and Goodwall will release "Powering the Future," our full report on the careers young people want to pursue, the businesses they want to build, and what they need to get started.
